candidate.educational_objective: Minimize CAUTI risk by removing an indwelling urinary catheter promptly once the clinical indication has ended.

options.A: Follow the applicable order or nurse-driven protocol to remove the catheter as soon as it is no longer needed
options.B: Leave the catheter in place for convenience until discharge
options.C: Keep the catheter until bacteriuria develops, then remove it
options.D: Replace the catheter with a new indwelling catheter on a fixed schedule even though no indication remains

candidate.rationale: CDC recommends inserting indwelling urinary catheters only for appropriate indications and leaving them in place only as long as needed. CDC implementation guidance specifically supports identifying and removing catheters that are no longer needed, including nurse-directed protocols.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Supports leaving urinary catheters in place only as long as needed and using systems/protocols to remove unnecessary catheters.
candidate.source_document_title: Guideline for Prevention of Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections — Summary of Recommendations
candidate.source_locator: I. Appropriate Urinary Catheter Use, I.A and IV.A
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
candidate.stem: An indwelling urinary catheter was inserted for hourly urine-output measurement while a client was critically ill. The client is now stable and no longer has an appropriate indication for the catheter. What should the nurse do?
